newsitem.title: USA: Foxmeyer Health faces creditors' suit.
newsitem.headline: Foxmeyer Health faces creditors' suit.

text.p: FoxMeyer Health Corp faces a $198 million fraud suit filed by the official unsecured creditors' committee of its units FoxMeyer Corp and FoxMeyer Drug Co, the committee's advisors said.
The committee is advised by the law firm of Dewey Ballantine and investment banking firm Alex Brown & Sons.

The suit seeks damanges for the allegedly fraudulent transfer of assets from FoxMeyer Corp and FoxMeyer Drug to FoxMeyer Health resulting from a restructuring undertaken by the units in June 1996, two months before they filed for Chapter 11.

The committee advisors said the suit alleges that the transfers were made at a time when FoxMeyer Corp and FoxMeyer Drug were insolvent, or rendered insolvent by the transactions, and left with "unreasonably" small capital to conduct their business.
The committee also charges that the units knew or should have known that the alleged transfers would leave them with debts they could not pay.
The suit alleges that the transfers were undertaken by FoxMeyer Health without any "legitimate business justification."
The advisors said the committee hopes that the suit will result in enhanced recoveries by unsecured creditors of FoxMeyer Corp and FoxMeyer Drug, who are owed about $450 million.

The advisors said the creditors are facing "huge losses" in light of the recent sale of FoxMeyer Drug's pharmaceutical distribution business to McKesson Corp, which, they said, yielded $20 million to FoxMeyer Corp and FoxMeyer Drug, net of secured debt.
Officials at FoxMeyer Health could not immediately be reached for comment.
